audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition balance sheet is paired with pre-acquisition owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Total debt increased by a computed $328.4 million, from $472.7 million at December 31, 2025 to $801.1 million at June 30, 2026; cash decreased by $317.3 million; PayneCrest cost $404.7 million net of cash acquired; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, while the bridge adds post-acquisition cash without deducting debt. The numerator therefore excludes both PayneCrest earnings and the full recurring financing cost associated with the post-acquisition capital structure.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $28.7 million compared to $65.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible risk. Missing PayneCrest earnings understates value, while using FY2025 interest expense of $28.7 million despite the new $411.8 million term borrowing can overstate value. The competing effects cannot be netted from the supplied record, but their scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a same-perimeter run using PayneCrest post-acquisition OE, normalized annual interest on the June 30 debt structure, acquisition-related amortization and recurring costs, and a bridge dated to that same period.

audit_findings.title: The single-year anchor depends on revenue whose price remains unapproved
audit_findings.magnitude: $179.5 million of unapproved contract-modification revenue recognized through December 31, 2025, equal to 65.8% of the $272.8 million OE anchor; the associated profit contribution is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uncollectible amount, price concession, cost underestimate, or reversal reduces normalized OE; because FY2025 OE is the sole anchor, that reduction propagates through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately $ 179.5 million of the unapproved contract modifications had been recognized as revenue on a cumulative catch-up basis through December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Recognition of the $179.5 million is demonstrated, but an eventual loss or reversal is not. The full revenue amount cannot be treated as an OE overstatement because related costs were incurred and only the after-tax profit or cash shortfall affects OE. Nevertheless, the exposure is large relative to the anchor, and June 2026 filings show $205.9 million of recognized unapproved modifications and $87.6 million of negative revenue estimate revisions concerning pre-2026 performance obligations, although the record does not attribute those revisions specifically to the FY2025 modifications. The uncertainty is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level recognized revenue, cost, gross profit, billings, collections, subsequent approvals and settlements for the FY2025 modifications; rerun after removing any unsupported after-tax profit and related uncollectible cash amount from the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require working capital not captured as reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: Contract assets increased $163.2 million during 2025 to $936.9 million; changes in assets and liabilities used $181.9 million and operating cash flow was negative $131.3 million in the first half of 2026; normalized omitted reinvestment is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental receivables, unbilled revenue and retainage consume cash needed to produce growth. If that investment is absent from OE or the RONTA reinvestment calculation, forecast distributable cash and terminal value are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Consequently, we have significant working capital invested in assets that may have a liquidation period extending beyond one year .
audit_findings.explanation: The substantial and sometimes long-dated working-capital commitment is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether normalized working capital was already incorporated into the OE or RONTA mechanics. The filed balances and cash-flow variability show that the possible omission is large enough to affect the 3% and 6% growth cases materially; the 0% bear case is less exposed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE formula and RONTA denominator to changes in receivables, contract assets, retainage, contract liabilities, payables and accruals; estimate normalized incremental working capital per dollar of growth over a full project cycle and rerun the growth cases.

audit_findings.title: A potentially significant pension claim is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered withdrawal or plan-termination liability would be a claim ahead of common equity and should be deducted in the equity bridge; increased recurring contributions would instead reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We participate in a number of multiemployer pension plans, and our potential withdrawal obligation may be significant.
audit_findings.explanation: No present omitted liability is demonstrated. The company reported no plan to withdraw, and the listed defined-benefit plans were in green status with no surcharge; the $68.2 million of 2025 contributions was already charged to contracts and therefore already affected earnings. The contingent withdrawal exposure cannot be estimated from the filing and becomes valuation-relevant if withdrawal, termination, deteriorating funding status or additional contribution requirements become probable.
audit_findings.action: Monitor current Form 5500 filings, funding notices, zone-status changes, contribution surcharges and labor or restructuring decisions; obtain plan-specific withdrawal estimates and rerun the bridge if a triggering event becomes probable or occurs.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 includes favorable project-closeout effects that may not recur
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring closeout gain embedded in FY2025 OE raises the sole anchor and is consequently capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Gross profit as a percentage of revenue increased to 11.5% in 2025 compared to 10.6% in 2024 primarily due to improved performance in power delivery and a favorable impact from project closeouts in gas operations in 2025, partially offset by a decline in higher margin storm work in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The favorable FY2025 closeout effect is demonstrated, and the June 2026 filing again identifies it as a reason Utilities margins declined year over year. However, the filing does not isolate its dollar contribution: Utilities gross margin rose from 10.6% in 2024 to 11.5% in 2025 for several offsetting reasons. The record therefore cannot establish the required OE adjustment or whether it is material after considering normal recurring closeout gains and losses.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level FY2025 closeout gains and losses, compare the net amount with a multi-year normalized level, calculate the after-tax OE difference, and rerun the valuation if the FY2025 anchor contains an exceptional net benefit.
